cells.tense: You're here at the start of something, and your eyes are open to it — before it's named, before it's proven, you can already see the shape of it.
cells.ask: Let yourself say the clear thing you see about what's growing here, and then let it stand without defending it.
cells.core:
There's a clarity in you that arrives before the arguing does. You don't have to force it or prove it — you can just see what you see and tend what's actually in front of you. When you're tending something small and new, you don't need to know how it will all turn out. You read the first green shoot correctly, water it, and step back. And when you look at what's growing — a person, a project, a life — the seeing and the giving come out of the same quiet place. You're not performing the care and you're not selling the vision. You just see it, and what you do next grows from that seeing.

The seeing doesn't need an audience. It only needs to be trusted — and you get to be the one who trusts it first.
cells.sheetLine: You see what's actually growing, and you tend it from that clear sight.
cells.verb: seeing clearly what's actually there before you decide what it means
cells.place: in the garden where what you tend is still coming up

cells.tense: You're already out ahead of it, looking at what it'll need next and the next after that, tending a future that hasn't arrived instead of what's in front of you now.
cells.ask: Let one thing you're growing be exactly what it is today, and don't reach for what it could become until it shows you.
cells.core:
You can't stop seeing the next version of everything. It hasn't even sprouted yet and you're already measuring the harvest, planning for what you'll have to do when it gets bigger. The planning feels like care, but the thing itself keeps getting interrupted by what it's supposed to become. A seedling with someone hovering over it doesn't grow faster — it grows to the shape of the hovering.

What you're doing comes from a real place. It just arrives early and loud, and the thing you're tending can't hear itself over your schedule for it. Stay in today and let today be enough.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending what it could become instead of what's here.

cells.tense: You stopped seeing clearly a while back, and you're still standing where that was true, tending on habit what you can't quite see anymore.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're actually responsible for, and move it one clear step forward today.
cells.core:
In the garden this is the morning walk where you know what needs water and what needs waiting. You don't have to force anything; you just give each thing what it actually needs and let it come. But something went quiet in you, and the seeing went with it. Now you're still out there doing the motions of care, but you can't tell if any of it is landing or if it ever did. The old clarity doesn't come when called, and forcing it just proves it's gone.

This isn't about caring harder. It's about picking up one real thing, with edges you can see, and moving it forward. The seeing comes back through your hands first.
cells.sheetLine: The seeing went quiet, but the care is still going through the motions.

cells.tense: You're seeing clearly right now — it's shaping every choice you make — but you talk about it like it's just something that happens to you.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've noticed that changed how you treated it, and claim that noticing as yours.
cells.core:
In the garden this is walking by and noticing the one leaf that curled — you water only that one, and it comes back. You read what each thing needs before it asks, and you adjust without making a project of it. That's the everyday shape of it when it's working, and it's working now.

But you don't give yourself credit for it. It feels like common sense or just being observant, so the actual insight never gets owned. No one assigned you that clear eye. You opened it and you've been using it. Say so where you can hear yourself say it.
cells.sheetLine: The clarity is already yours. You keep calling it nothing special.
